name: Range View
award: 2024 Federal 9% and state housing tax credits (Round One)
headline: Northwest Real Estate Capital Corp. and the Saguache County Housing Authority built Range View, 32 family apartments at 30% to 60% AMI at 250 Gunnison Ave. in the Town of Saguache, on housing authority land, with a 2024 Round One 9% and state credit award from CHFA; a grand opening was set for 2026-09-17.
why_it_matters: It shows how a very small rural county (about 6,500 people) closed a roughly $16.1M 9% deal: a nonprofit developer partnered with the housing authority for a nominal ground lease, and a DOLA Strong Communities grant paid for the water line, hydrants and paving the town could not fund.

status.label: Grand opening scheduled 2026-09-17; move-ins expected from September 2026
status.detail: Groundbreaking was held on 2025-07-09. Applications opened in June 2026, and the county housing authority page says move-ins were expected to begin the first week of September 2026 (while noting the building was still under construction). Heart of the Rockies Radio reported on 2026-09-16 that the grand opening and ribbon cutting would be held the next day. No record of a certificate of occupancy or occupancy level was found.

next_step: Watch for a report of the 2026-09-17 ribbon cutting and CHFA's placed-in-service record.

key_numbers.value: 32 family apartments, all at 30% to 60% AMI
key_numbers.meaning: 7 at 30%, 7 at 40%, 11 at 50% and 7 at 60% AMI; the 60% units are underwritten at 50% rents, per the applicant.

key_numbers.value: $1,340,823 a year in federal 9% credit plus $700,000 of state credit
key_numbers.meaning: About $13.4M in federal credit over 10 years (inferred). The applicant had requested $1,450,000 a year.
Awarded to Saguache County in April 2024 for off-site infrastructure; the county agreed to a 20% match of up to $200,000.
The Crestone Eagle reported the project fully funded at $16.1 million in July 2024, about $503,000 per unit (inferred).

background.text: The site began as a 26-unit concept the Saguache County Housing Authority worked up through CHFA's Small Scale Housing Technical Assistance program, with five public meetings; Northwest then joined as developer and the plan grew to 32 units. A local resident suggested the name.
The two partners earlier developed The Iron Horse in Alamosa together, and the housing authority already manages two small properties in Saguache (12 Section 8 units and 16 HOME units).

The applicant said a 4% deal was not workable here because of the rural location, small unit count and low incomes in the market area; the market study gave capture rates of 8.3% (primary) and 4.5% (extended).

Rural cost drivers named by the applicant: a sprinkler system the existing water lines could not serve (no full-time fire department), two new hydrants, paving of the alley and 2nd Street, an elevation of 7,703 feet with a short building season, and few local contractors.
The environmental report found no issues but noted possible remains of a razed house and a gravel pile, to be handled by a soils management plan.
Construction was planned to run from July 2025 to the end of August 2026, per the groundbreaking announcement.

discrepancies.text: The application narrative lists 14 one-bedroom, 12 two-bedroom and 6 three-bedroom units (32), while CHFA's award description lists only 14 one-bedroom and 12 two-bedroom units (26) for the 32-unit project.
CHFA's award report names the sponsor Northwest Real Estate Capital Corp., while its award description names Northwest Real Estate Development Capital Corp.

The application narrative says Range View would be the first tax credit property ever built in Saguache County, while CHFA's award description calls it the first tax credit development in the county in over 25 years (the narrative itself lists four tax credit properties in Center, the most recent from 1998).
